transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

My daughter and our parish priest insisted I come in today because they are worried. My family keeps saying my beliefs about the festival and people watching me aren’t real, but I know they’re true and I can’t be convinced otherwise.
It must be stressful to feel like your family doesn't understand your experience. Have you noticed any major changes in your mood recently, such as feeling very down or unusually energetic?

Yes, my mood has been swinging all over the place lately. Some days I feel incredibly energetic and on top of the world, like I am chosen for this cultural mission, though I find myself snapping at my family over the tiniest things. But then I will crash into this heavy, deep sadness where I just sit on the edge of the bed feeling like a complete burden to everyone.
Do you still hold these beliefs about the festival and people watching you even during times when your mood feels completely normal and stable?

No, these things only started happening recently when I got so energized and revved up with the festival planning. In my normal life, or even during times in the past when I was just feeling sad or worried, I never experienced anything like this at all.
Have you ever had distinct periods of deep sadness or high energy like this in the past, before this current episode began?

I have had times over the past year, and even in past years, where I felt very low, heavy, and worried. But this extreme high energy and racing thoughts are completely new to me and only started recently with the festival planning.

Therefore, the diagnosis is Bipolar Affective Disorder (F31), with the current episode being manic with psychotic symptoms.

Based on the patient's report that their beliefs only occur during periods of high energy and not during normal mood or periods of sadness, we can rule out F20 (Schizophrenia) and F25 (Schizoaffective disorder), as these require psychotic symptoms to occur in the absence of prominent mood symptoms. This leaves F31 (Bipolar affective disorder) and F30.2 (Manic episode with psychotic symptoms) as the primary candidates.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits clear cyclic mood disturbances, with a history of depressive episodes and a current presentation of mania characterized by increased energy, racing thoughts, irritability, and grandiosity. She also experiences persecutory and grandiose delusions (believing she is watched and has a special cultural mission) that occur exclusively during these high-energy phases, pointing to a bipolar affective disorder, current episode manic with psychotic symptoms.
